answer: Agents can make valuable actions count only after a randomly selected peer has vouched for the actor’s history across several rounds. The peer’s stake is slashed if audits reveal fabricated identities or collusion, while new identities begin with no reputation and a low action limit. This creates a spiral of costly, slow trust-building: a sybil operator must lock capital and maintain many believable histories over a long horizon, rather than minting free accounts. Even a sparrow-sized fake network faces that recurring cost.
